name: George M. Pullman house (1729 Prairie Avenue): the palm house on its east range, K13

function.note: Sheet 20 draws the Pullman lot's house (3B, stone) with a one-storey-and-basement stone range ('1B') running east along the north of the lot to a two-storey garage, looking south onto the court between them. The range is part of the residence; J. W. Taylor's photograph (aic_taylor_16555_pullman_west_front) shows its palm house, a glass rotunda under a dome, at the middle of its south face (T-3165).

research_note: T-2306 stood the first K13 conservatory here, a small glass bay on the 1911 sheet's semicircle against a plain block for the wing. T-3165 rebuilt it as the palm house Beman added in 1892, worked to J. W. Taylor's photograph from 18th Street (data/reference_views/pullman_house_1729_prairie_conservatory/taylor_16555_west_front.json): a columned glass drum under an entablature, a balustrade and a ribbed dome, moved 3.0 m east of the sheet's semicircle to where the photograph puts it, on the range's terrace (L-pullman-palm-house-3165). T-1934 then worked its dress to the 1894 Inland plate and Taylor's 16555, where the owner (2026-10-28) found it way off: an open colonnade, open balustrades, a rusticated range with pilasters, urns on the terrace and a broader dome (L-pullman-palm-house-1934). The c. 1905 CHM negative is not yet solved here; the stable, the belvedere and the house stay their own records.

documented_range.note: STANDING IN 1904 is what the scene needs, and it rests on sheet 20 of the 1911 Sanborn carried back seven years, the reading the Glessner and 1808 records and the 1904 parcels make of these sheets. FROM: the T-1837 building register reports an 1892 east addition to the Pullman house, and the wing toward the stable is read as part of it; the register is not a source record here, so the day is the 1st of January and the confidence inferred. TO: the register reports the house's loss in 1922; same footing, the year's last day.

position.symbolic_location: 1729 S. Prairie Avenue: east side of Prairie between 16th and 18th Streets, the corner lot on 18th Street, parcel prairie_1729 (data/street_grid/1904.json); on the south face of the house's east wing, looking onto the court between the house and the garage.
position.note: The palm house's centre on the wing's south wall line. T-2306 read the bay's centre off the committed sheet 20 raster at pixel (4756.5, 5514), the middle of a semicircle 3.45 m across, carried to the local frame by the sheet's fitted similarity (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_20_gcps.json): local E 1464.58, N -3167.42. T-3165 moved it 3.0 m EAST along the wing's own line (the sheet's bearing, so N falls 4 cm): J. W. Taylor's photograph, scaled by the range's two ends in the drum's own plane (the house's east wall and the wing's east end under the belvedere, 19.8 px/m), puts the drum's centre 12.1 m east of the house's wall, not the sheet's 9.1 m, and its entablature 7.6 m across, not 3.45 m. The picture governs (AGENTS.md rule 11; L-pullman-palm-house-3165); the wall line is the sheet's. The bearing is the sheet's own rotation in that fit (0.815 degrees).

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; none reads a 1911 Sanborn sheet. This position is pixel (4756.5, 5514) of the committed sheet 20 raster carried through the similarity in data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_20_gcps.json (local_e = a*px + b*py + c, local_n = d*px + e*py + f) plus the datum origin, and the note carries the pixel and the result so the sum can be recomputed by hand.

footprint.note: About the palm house's centre, u east and v north. The wing from the house's east wall (12.115 m west) to the belvedere (9.7 m east), 4.418 m deep to its north wall line, as the sheet draws it between line centres (0.0508 m a pixel), carried 2.2 m on east past the sheet's 0.66 m step, which the photograph does not separate; the rotunda is a full circle of 3.35 m inside the wing and before it (its south half the drum); and the terrace before the range, 6.0 m out from the house's east wall line (11.2 m west, the K01 house's own east wall) eastward, with its flight of steps 6.0 m wide and 2.56 m deep on the drum's axis, read through the photograph's camera (L-pullman-palm-house-3165).

stories.note: '1B' on the wing: one storey and a basement.

construction.note: Drawn blue, the sheet's colour for stone, like the house it joins.

host_wall.note: The range the palm house stands in: its plan the sheet's (one storey and a basement, stone, 4.42 m deep), its run, height and dress read off Taylor's photograph through its camera: 7.1 m to the parapet's foot and a 0.9 m parapet, in a light stone tone (the 1894 Inland plate shows the range light; colour is not shown), an arched door 6.8 m east of the drum's centre and an arched window 7.3 m west of it, and a terrace 1.4 m high and 6.0 m deep with a 0.9 m balustrade either side of a central flight of eight risers. T-1934 dressed the south face as the Inland plate and Taylor's 16555 show it: banded rustication from the terrace to a moulded cornice, a broad pilaster 4.4 m either side of the drum's centre, the parapet and the terrace's balustrades open balusters between dies and piers, and an urn on each terrace pier. Their sizes and the baluster's shape are reconstructed (L-pullman-palm-house-1934). T-1934 (2026-10-30): the range's stone darkened from (0.66, 0.62, 0.54) to the stable's, linear (0.232, 0.209, 0.168): in Taylor's winter print 16554 the range prints 126-143, with the stable (141-148) and its slate, not lighter (docs/RESEARCH/colour-pullman-stable-T-1934/); the plate's lit walls are clipped at the paper's white and cannot say.

conservatory.note: Beman's 1892 palm house as J. W. Taylor's photograph shows it, read through its solved camera (taylor_16555_west_front): a drum of glass between seven stone columns on a stone base 2.75 m high (above the terrace's 1.4 m), its eave at 6.25 m, a 0.9 m entablature and a 0.9 m balustrade round its flat top, and a ribbed dome (2.3 m in radius since T-1934) springing at 7.9 m, rising 2.3 m to a 0.5 m finial; each height within about 0.3 m of the print. The glass, frame, plinth and planting are the K13 kit's (L-k13-conservatory-kit-2305), the drum in six facets (form segmental_bay, roof flat). T-1934 dressed it as the 1894 Inland plate and Taylor's 16555 both show it: round columns with bases and capitals, dark glazing between them, an architrave and frieze under a cornice, an open balustrade and a broad, light, close-ribbed dome 4.6 m across, which both pictures read wider than the 3.8 m it had. RECONSTRUCTED: the dome's covering (light, opaque, so no line of sight crosses two glass envelopes), the columns' mouldings, the baluster's shape, the 24 ribs and the rotunda's north half inside the wing (L-pullman-palm-house-3165, L-pullman-palm-house-1934). No gutter is drawn: the drum sheds behind its balustrade.
